## Common Pricing Mistake

Here's the problem with that approach. A bulleted list doesn't sell anything on its
own. Your potential client is not simply buying a certain number of images or a
certain number of hours with you.

They are making a financial decision based on an experience with you. Are you
thinking about your photography business like that? Are you thinking about it as
being an experience?

You're not just selling product, you are selling a service. And so people need to
have a buy in with that type of a business. And so if you're not thinking about
your photography business as a service and experience, that's the first thing that
you need to change in your mindset.

You need to change how you approach your photography packages. Before someone can
feel good about saying yes, they need to actually understand what they are
investing in, not just what they're getting, but why it matters and what it's going
to feel like to go through an experience with you. Try to picture it from a client
side for a second.

They open your message or your email on their phone. They see the two or three

That's all of the information you are giving them to help them decide if they want

## Explain Package Value

The second thing I want you to look at is, does your potential client understand
exactly what they are getting and why it matters? This is where so many
photographers stop short. And I totally understand why.

It feels efficient to just list out the basics. Location, outfits, number of images,
done. But that only tells someone what is technically included.

It doesn't tell them who this specific package is actually built for, or what the
entire experience is going to look like from the very first step all the way through
to receiving their finished gallery. Walk them through it like you are explaining it
to a friend. Tell them what a typical session actually feels like, from the moment
they arrive to the moment it wraps up.

Tell them what the gallery delivery experience is like when it arrives in their
inbox and what it feels like to scroll through it for the first time. Tell them what
kind of client usually chooses this particular package and why it fits their life so
well, whether that is a family who wants a shorter, simpler session or a senior who
wants the full experience with multiple outfits and location options. When someone
reads through your package description, they should be able to see themselves inside
of that package.

They should be able to picture their own kid, their own living room, their own
senior year, showing up somewhere in that description. That is really the whole
point of what you are writing. And not only does an investment guide showcase the
session, but again, it's got so many different elements that is going to be a
conversion tool for your lead.

So they're getting to see things visually. They're getting to learn who it's for and
how one package differs from another. They're still getting that bulleted list, but
they're getting things that actually matter to them.

It's not just random things thrown in a bulleted list. They're able to see your

## Profitable Pricing Check

This one is a little less about how things are presented and a lot more about the
numbers behind your prices. Is each package genuinely profitable for you? Once you
account for your time and your expenses, is it genuinely valuable for the client on
the other end?

And just as important, is there real noticeable separation between your packages so
that moving up from one tier to the next actually feels like a meaningful upgrade?
If you've been a listener of the podcast for a long time, you know how important
pricing for profit is. I have a pricing for profit formula freebie that you can run
your numbers through if you need help making sure that you are actually profitable.

I know sitting down and looking at the numbers in your business can be stressful,
and it's something that you would rather just avoid, but you need to know the data.
I want you to sit down this week and do a pricing check-in with yourself. Look at
the real data and try to set your emotions to the side.

Here's a signal I really want you to pay attention to going forward. If you're
getting a healthy number of leads, but they are not converting into bookings and you
are confident that it is not a quality issue with your actual photography, then it
is almost always your pricing and packaging waving a red flag at you. And I want to
be clear, it does not automatically mean you need to lower your prices.

Sometimes the fix is restructuring what's included inside each package. Sometimes
it's clarifying exactly who each package was built for. So the decision in front of
your clients feel obvious instead of overwhelming.
